newsitem.title: USA: Texaco replaces 113 pct of reserves in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Texaco replaces 113 pct of reserves in 1996.

text.p: Texaco Inc said it replaced 113 percent of its combined oil and natural gas reserves in 1996, with gains in international reserves preventing its reserve base from contracting.
In a prepared statement, the company said international reserve replacements were 154 percent, compared to just 83 percent domestically.

The company noted that 87 percent of such reserve additions were in extensions, new sands, and enhanced recovery operations, with the majority of the additions coming from activities in the United Kingdom North Sea, the Caribbean island Trindad, Indonesia, Colombia and the U.S.

Texaco said that as of year-end 1996, it had 3.7 billion barrels of oil equivalent of worldwide net proved reserves consisting of 2.7 billion barrels of liquid reserves and six trillion cubic feet of net proved gas reserves.
"These figures represent the fourth consecutive year that Texaco has replaced more than 100 percent of our worldwide production annually," Texaco Chief Exective Peter Bijur said in the statement.
Barrels of oil equivalent are calculated by dividing billions of cubic feet of natural gas by six and adding it to million barrels of crude and natural gas liquids.
In the three-year 1994-1996 period, worldwide reserve replacement has averaged 118 percent, with finding and development costs averaging $3.89 per barrel of oil equivalent, Texaco said.
The five year average from 1992-1996 of reserve replacement was 112 percent, with costs averaging $4.04 per barrel of oil equivalent, the company said.
The total figures include equity reserves in affiliates.
